beats.narration_text: Hola, I'm Muh-yunk, and this is my final project pitch. It starts with one question. Can a support bot answer policy questions from a current source?

show.event: types 'Can a support bot answer policy questions safely'
'safely' is deleted and retyped as 'from a current source'

qc.sparse_reason: Hesitant-writer bookend: the correction is the motion.

beats.narration_text: Three terms. A policy answer: anything a bot tells a customer about refunds, fees, or eligibility. A source: the dated policy document that answer relies on. And a hold: the answer waits for a person instead of being sent.

terms.meaning: the bot's claims about refunds, fees, eligibility
the dated policy behind the reply
the reply waits until staff decide

qc.sparse_reason: Terms card: three prerequisites, one line each.

beats.narration_text: This really happened. In 2024, a Canadian tribunal ruled on a case against Air Canada. The airline's chatbot told a customer he could claim a bereavement fare after he travelled. The policy said the request had to come before. The tribunal held the airline responsible for its chatbot.

beats.narration_text: So my project is Source Check for Support AI. It will sit between a support bot and the customer, and check every policy answer against the company's current policy before it is sent.

shot.visual_intent: The same conveyor, now with a checkpoint scanner arch over it; label 'Source Check'.

beats.narration_text: Step one. Claude will break the bot's answer into claims, like 'refund after travel', and return them in a fixed format that my code checks before using them.

beats.narration_text: Step two. Python code, not the model, will look up the current, dated version of the policy, and compare each claim with it: the numbers, the dates, and conditions like before or after.

beats.narration_text: If every claim matches, the answer goes out, and a log records which policy version it relied on.

beats.narration_text: If a claim has no source, relies on an outdated version, or contradicts the policy, the answer is held. A person sees the reason in Slack and decides.

shot.visual_intent: The parcel is diverted to a human handoff desk; label 'HOLD'; a person marker appears.
shot.motion_claim: The parcel is diverted to a human handoff desk; label 'HOLD'; a person marker appears.

beats.narration_text: An n8n workflow will run all of this: answer in, check, then pass or hold. It works in front of any bot, so it doesn't replace one.

shot.visual_intent: The answer box sits between a 'pass' tray and a 'hold' tray; it slides into 'hold'.
shot.motion_claim: The answer box sits between a 'pass' tray and a 'hold' tray; it slides into 'hold'.

beats.narration_text: I looked at three alternatives: Intercom Fin, Zendesk's AI agents, and manual review of transcripts. The two products answer from your help content and hand off to people. Manual review happens after the answer is sent. What I didn't find on their public pages is a check of each answer against the current policy version before it goes out.

beats.narration_text: Who opens it? A hiring manager for an AI automation engineer. In the first minute they'll run one command and watch an outdated refund answer get held, with the reason.

beats.narration_text: What it will prove: prompt contracts, source grounding, verification, approval gates, and evaluation. The evidence will be tests and a labelled test set, with the miss rate reported. It won't prove it's ready for production.

shot.visual_intent: An evidence binder opens; test pages and an evaluation page come out.

beats.narration_text: The scope. It will only check policy answers for one fictional company, on synthetic data. It won't write answers. The first piece will be the checker and one test: the Air Canada case must come out held.

shot.visual_intent: An experiment bench; one test sample slides in; a terracotta light comes on.

beats.narration_text: What could sink it: a dropped condition word. If extraction turns before into after, a wrong answer could pass. So uncertain answers will default to hold, and my test set will be full of condition flips.

shot.visual_intent: An inspection lamp swings onto a claim page; labels 'before' and 'after'.

beats.narration_text: Why this project? I've already built n8n workflows with Claude in my public repos. What's new for me is building an evaluation set and measuring the misses. And Week one taught me that a confident answer isn't a checked one.
